persons.name: Viśvaratna
persons.evidence: liṣitaṃ taṃrāchitola jhvābāhārayā varjācāryya viśvaratnaṃ coyā thaota dayakā tayā

date.as_written: samvat 1021 mti phārguna śukla pūrṇṇemā ṣunaṃ

purpose: svārtha: the scribe wrote it for himself (thaota dayakā tayā); a curse warns others against taking it away
notes: "varjācāryya" is a scribal metathesis of vajrācārya. Taṃrāchi Ṭola and Jhvābāhāra (Jhvā Bahā) are probably in Kathmandu, but I left the normalized place empty because that isn't certain. "ṣunaṃ" after pūrṇṇemā probably stands for "khunhu" (day). I don't read it as a weekday. "thaota" = "thao-ta" (for oneself), so the scribe was also the intended owner. The colophon's date agrees with the catalogue date (NS 1021). The catalogue gives no scribe; the colophon names Viśvaratna.
